    {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [IsPartialCube G] (h_helly : OppositeSemicubeHellyProperty G) :
    IsAntipodal G ↔ PairwiseIsomorphicOppositeSemicubes G
directions.proof_strategy: Formalize partial cubes as isometric subgraphs of hypercubes, define the Djoković-Winkler relation Θ and Θ-classes, formalize semicubes W_ab and W_ba, define antipodal graphs and the opposite-semicube Helly property. Prove the forward direction by showing antipodality implies isomorphic opposite semicubes. For the reverse direction, assume the Helly property and isomorphic opposite semicubes, then construct an antipodal mapping using the non-empty intersections guaranteed by the Helly property to show every vertex has a unique antipode.
directions.title: Antipodality Characterization via Opposite-Semicube Helly Property

directions.description: For a geometric family of principally polarized abelian varieties over Q, the average size of the ℓ-Selmer group is unbounded if and only if the product of local Tamagawa ratios exceeds 1. Specifically, for the family of quadratic twists {E_d : d squarefree} of an elliptic curve E/Q at a prime ℓ of good reduction, the average |Sel_ℓ(E_d)| over |d| ≤ X is unbounded as X → ∞ if and only if ∏_p c_p(E, ℓ) > 1, where c_p(E, ℓ) is the local factor from the Greenberg–Wiles formula. The paper proves this for families with constant ℓ-torsion Galois module; the conjecture asserts it holds unconditionally.

Use the Greenberg-Wiles formula to express |Sel_ℓ(A)|/|Sel_ℓ(A^∨)^∨| = ∏_p c_p. For principally polarized varieties, the Cassels pairing gives |Sel_ℓ(A)| ≥ √(∏_p c_p). The key step is showing that the dual Selmer correction factor is bounded on average across the family, using the character sum and ramification section machinery developed in the paper to control the discrepancy between the local lower bound and the true Selmer size.

directions.description: For every elliptic curve E/Q with analytic rank 0 and every non-trivial finite abelian group G, there exist infinitely many G-extensions F/Q such that E(F) is finite (equivalently, rank E(F) = 0). This removes the 'no exceptional primes' condition from the paper's Corollary 1.3 and the 'sufficiently large prime factors' condition from Theorem 1.1, yielding the full generalization of the David-Fearnley-Kisilevsky conjecture from quadratic to all finite abelian extensions.

The key obstacle is removing the 'exceptional prime' and 'sufficiently large prime factor' hypotheses from the horizontal p-adic L-function machinery. This likely requires: (1) refined analysis of local root numbers at all primes dividing the conductor to control the sign in the functional equation uniformly across all twists, and (2) overcoming the limitation that current horizontal p-adic L-function techniques require p to be large relative to the level to ensure Eisenstein-type congruences dominate the residual spectrum.

directions.description: A tournament T is cycle Mengerian (CM) if for every nonnegative integral weight function w on arcs, the maximum cycle packing size ν_w(T) equals its fractional relaxation ν*_w(T). T is cycle ideal (CI) if the minimum feedback arc set weight τ_w(T) equals its fractional relaxation τ*_w(T) for all such w. Since ν*_w = τ*_w by LP duality, CM and CI together yield the min-max relation τ_w = ν_w. The conjecture is that these two integrality properties coincide: a tournament is CM if and only if it is CI.

directions.proof_strategy: Show that for tournaments, the FAS LP constraint matrix is totally unimodular on CM instances, and vice versa. Use the structural characterization of CM tournaments by Chen et al. (2020) to verify that every CM tournament satisfies the CI property (τ*_w = τ_w) by exhibiting integral optimal solutions to the FAS LP, and conversely that every CI tournament satisfies the CM property by showing the cycle packing LP has integral optima. The key bridge is the LP duality equality ν*_w = τ*_w and the chain of inequalities ν_w ≤ ν*_w = τ*_w ≤ τ_w.
directions.title: Cycle Mengerian and Cycle Ideal Equivalence for Tournaments

directions.description: The paper proves that a countable FAC poset P satisfies the Aharoni-Korman conjecture if P contains no saturated chain D such that either D or its reverse D* is of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x, where each D_x is infinite and co-wellfounded. The conjecture asserts that this condition is also necessary: if a countable FAC poset P does contain such a saturated chain, then P fails to satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture. This would yield a complete characterization of which countable FAC posets satisfy the Aharoni-Korman conjecture.

The construction likely involves adapting the known counterexamples to the original Aharoni-Korman conjecture, using the specific structure of ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x to control all possible chain-antichain interactions.
directions.title: Necessity of the forbidden chain condition for the Aharoni-Korman conjecture on countable FAC posets

directions.description: For any convex polytope P in ℝ^� (with e = d+1 being the embedding dimension), the set of centerpoints of P coincides with the floating body of P at level 1/(d+1). Specifically, a point x is a centerpoint of P (meaning every closed halfspace containing x contains at least a 1/(d+1) fraction of the volume of P) if and only if x belongs to the floating body F_{1/(d+1)}(P), defined as the intersection of all closed halfspaces H⁺ such that vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ (1/(d+1)) · vol(P). The paper establishes this equivalence and further shows that for polytopes this set is semialgebraic.
domain_bridges: Convex geometry ↔ Combinatorial topology ↔ Semialgebraic geometry ↔ Measure theory on polytopes

 sorry
directions.proof_strategy: The proof proceeds by double inclusion. (⊆): If x is a centerpoint, then every halfspace H⁺ containing x satisfies vol(P ∩ H⁺) ≥ vol(P)/(d+1), equivalently vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ vol(P)·d/(d+1); but the floating body condition requires vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ vol(P)/(d+1) for the halfspaces defining it, so one must show that a centerpoint lies in every halfspace whose complementary cap has volume ≤ vol(P)/(d+1). (⊇): Conversely, if x ∈ F_{1/(d+1)}(P), then x lies in every halfspace H⁺ with vol(P \ H⁺) ≤ vol(P)/(d+1), and one must show this forces every halfspace through x to capture at least 1/(d+1) of the volume. The key technical ingredient is that the cap-volume function is piecewise rational on the arrangement of oriented hyperplanes determined by the polytope's facets, which makes both sets explicitly semialgebraic and allows their coincidence to be verified.
directions.title: Centerpoint-Floating Body Equivalence for Convex Polytopes

directions.description: For a squarefree integer N > 1 with an even number of prime factors, and a positive divisor d | N, let w_d denote the corresponding Atkin-Lehner involution on the Shimura curve X_N. The genus of the quotient X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ is determined by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula applied to the double cover X_N → X_N / ⟨w_d⟩, where the number of fixed points of w_d equals the number of optimal embeddings of a certain quadratic order into the quaternion order, expressible via class numbers. The conjecture is: X_N / ⟨w_d⟩ has genus zero if and only if (N, d) belongs to an explicit finite list, which strictly contains the list {(6,6), (10,10), (22,22)} arising from genus-zero X_N alone. This classification is the key structural result enabling the extension of the Giampietro-Darmon factorization beyond the original conjecture.

directions.proof_strategy: First formalize the genus formula for Shimura curves X_N of discriminant N (already explicit in the literature, e.g., Ogg). Then formalize the fixed-point count of Atkin-Lehner involutions w_d in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders via optimal embedding counts. Apply Riemann-Hurwitz to the double cover X_N → X_N/⟨w_d⟩ to obtain the genus of the quotient. Finally, enumerate all pairs (N, d) with N squarefree, ω(N) even, d | N, for which the resulting genus is zero, yielding the explicit finite classification.
directions.title: Genus-Zero Classification of Atkin-Lehner Quotients of Shimura Curves

directions.description: A Δ-matroid (E, F) is strong (i.e., satisfies the symmetric exchange axiom: for all A, B ∈ F and e ∈ A\B, there exists f ∈ B\A such that A △ {e,f} ∈ F and B △ {e,f} ∈ F) if and only if it contains no peerless antipode. Here, an antipode of a feasible set A with respect to an element e is a feasible set B obtained from A by exchanging e for some f, and a peerless antipode is one that is unique in a specific local sense within the feasible set system. This equivalence provides a local obstruction characterization for the global symmetric exchange property, analogous to how local submodularity characterizes global submodularity for rank functions.
domain_bridges: Tropical geometry (peerless antipode equations as tropicalization of orthogonal Grassmannian quadratics)

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Forward direction (strong ⟹ no peerless antipode): Assume symmetric exchange holds and suppose for contradiction that a peerless antipode exists at some feasible set A with element e. Use the symmetric exchange property between A and any other feasible set witnessing the peerless configuration to construct a second antipode, contradicting peerlessness. Backward direction (no peerless antipode ⟹ strong): Assume no peerless antipode exists and suppose symmetric exchange fails for some A, B ∈ F with e ∈ A\B. Show that the failure produces a peerless antipode: the element e at A has at most one viable exchange partner f ∈ B\A with A △ {e,f} ∈ F, and the absence of any other witness forces this antipode to be peerless, contradicting the hypothesis.
directions.title: Strong Δ-matroids are characterized by the absence of peerless antipodes

The proof then proceeds by showing that graphs violating the conclusion have a specific block structure that forces a long cycle.

This would establish the diameter bound via the triangle inequality. Alternatively, use structural induction on n and g, verifying that the bound holds for base cases and that any valid chord swap preserves the bound.

directions.description: For any split connected reductive group G over Q_p with Borel subgroup B and maximal torus T, the trianguline variety Y^{tri}(G) is Cohen-Macaulay. This strengthens the normality results established by Breuil-Hellmann-Schraen (for GL_n) and generalized in this paper (to arbitrary split reductive G, at certain points outside the smooth locus). Since Y^{tri}(G) is smooth of dimension dim(B) = dim(T) + |Φ^+| over the regular locus, Cohen-Macaulayness would follow from Serre's criterion (S2) combined with (R1) regularity in codimension 1. The (S2) condition is the deeper claim: for every point x ∈ Y^{tri}(G) with local ring O_{Y^{tri},x}, and every regular sequence f_1,...,f_d in the maximal ideal, the quotient O_{Y^{tri},x}/(f_1,...,f_d) has depth exactly d. This would imply the existence of well-behaved dualizing complexes and resolve the singularities of Y^{tri}(G) in the sense of local Langlands.

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Step 1: Formalize the trianguline variety Y^{tri}(G) as a rigid analytic space parameterizing trianguline G-representations with their triangulation data, using the Tannakian formalism for Rep_L(G) developed in the paper. Step 2: Establish that Y^{tri}(G) is regular in codimension ≤ 1 (condition R1) by analyzing the singular locus—its complement is the smooth regular locus characterized by the regularity of the triangulation parameter δ: T(Z_p) → T(E), and the singular locus has codimension ≥ 2 by dimension counting via the root structure of G. Step 3: Prove condition (S2) by showing that for every point x with codim ≥ 2, the local ring O_{Y^{tri},x} satisfies depth ≥ min(2, dim O_{Y^{tri},x}), using the crystallinity criterion for (φ,Γ)-modules with G-structure established in the paper to control the local equations. Step 4: Apply Serre's criterion (R1 + S2 ⟹ normal + CM for equidimensional schemes) to conclude.
directions.title: Cohen-Macaulay Property of the Trianguline Variety for Reductive Groups

directions.description: Let K/k be a finitely generated field extension of characteristic zero. Let G be a semiabelian variety over K, and let f: X → G be a finite morphism from a projective variety X of general type. Then the set X(K) of K-rational points is not Zariski dense in X. This extends the recent theorem of Xie-Yuan and Gao (which proves the case where G is an abelian variety) to the broader class of semiabelian varieties — extensions of abelian varieties by algebraic tori G_m^n. The principal new difficulty is the non-compactness of the torus component, which disrupts both the Nevanlinna-theoretic construction of entire curves from high-height rational points and the height theory used in the Vojta dictionary.

    {k K : Type*} [CommRing k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (hk : CharP k 0) (hK : IsFinitelyGenerated K k)
    {G : SemiabelianVariety K} {X : ProjectiveVariety K}
    (hX : IsGeneralType X) {f : X ⟶ G}
    (hf : IsFinite f) :
    ¬IsZariskiDense X (X.rationalPoints K) := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Adapt the Vojta dictionary framework of Xie-Yuan from abelian to semiabelian varieties in three stages. (1) Reduce to the case where X contains no translate of a positive-dimensional semiabelian subvariety, using the known Mordell-Lang theorem for semiabelian varieties over function fields (McQuillan, 1995). (2) Develop a toric height theory that controls the growth of Néron-Tate heights on the G_m^n component, analogous to the abelian variety height machine but accounting for logarithmic singularities at the boundary of the compactification. (3) Extend the Nevanlinna theory arguments to construct entire curves in complex fibers from high-height rational points, using logarithmic defect relations for non-compact targets. The key technical challenge is that entire curves in G_m^n can accumulate at the boundary, requiring logarithmic Nevanlinna theory with value distribution estimates for meromorphic functions with essential singularities at the torus boundary.
directions.title: Geometric Bombieri-Lang Conjecture for Finite Covers of Semiabelian Varieties

directions.description: There exists a matroid M on a finite ground set E and unordered pairs of bases {B₁, B₂} and {B₁', B₂'} of M such that the multiset union of B₁ and B₂ equals the multiset union of B₁' and B₂', yet no sequence of symmetric exchanges transforms {B₁, B₂} into {B₁', B₂'}. This formalizes the counterexample to Farber's conjecture (the s=2 case of White's conjecture part (ii)) presented in the paper, which disproves the widely-believed symmetric exchange connectivity property for unordered pairs of matroid bases.

      M.IsBasis B₁ ∧ M.IsBasis B₂ ∧ M.IsBasis B₁' ∧ M.IsBasis B₂' ∧
      (B₁.1 + B₂.1 : Multiset α) = (B₁'.1 + B₂'.1 : Multiset α) ∧
      ¬symmetric_exchange_reachable M {B₁, B₂} {B₁', B₂'} := by
  sorry

The finiteness of the state space (the set of unordered pairs of bases with the same multiset union) makes exhaustive search feasible, and the symmetric exchange graph can be constructed and checked for disconnected components.
directions.title: Farber's Conjecture Fails: A Matroid Counterexample to the Symmetric Exchange Property for Pairs of Bases

directions.description: For a finite nonempty poset P, the probabilistic powerdomain V₁(P) — the probability simplex on P ordered by the stochastic order — is an RB-domain if and only if P has a least element and the undirected Hasse graph of P is a tree. This encompasses two failure modes: (1) if P lacks a least element, the face of probability measures supported on minimal points is fixed pointwise by every deflation below the identity; (2) if the Hasse graph contains a cycle, the local stochastic cone becomes non-simplicial, precluding the finite-valued monotone approximations required by the RB property.

convex_geometry ↔ domain_theory: simplicial structure of local stochastic cones enables/disables deflation constructions
graph_theory ↔ order_theory: tree property of undirected Hasse graph characterizes deflation-existence

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Split into two directions. Forward (necessity): prove the contrapositive via two obstructions. Obstruction 1: if P has no least element, every deflation r ≤ id fixes the face of probability measures on minimal points pointwise, so no directed family of deflations can approximate the identity. Obstruction 2: if P has a least element but the Hasse graph has a cycle, the local stochastic cone at the Dirac measure on the least element is non-simplicial; a Euclidean finite-step cone argument then shows no finite-valued monotone approximation exists. Backward (sufficiency): given P with least element and tree Hasse graph, construct explicit directed family of deflations on V₁(P) with pointwise supremum the identity, using inductive decomposition along the tree structure.
directions.title: Probabilistic powerdomain RB-domain characterization for finite posets

directions.description: The paper proves that the Aharoni-Korman conjecture holds for countable FAC posets containing no saturated chain D such that D or its reverse is of the form ⨁ D_x (where each D_x is infinite and co-wellfounded). Since any well-founded poset cannot contain such a chain D (as it would entail an infinite descending chain), the theorem implies the conjecture holds for all countable well-founded FAC posets. This conjecture proposes that the result extends to uncountable cardinals: every well-founded poset with no infinite antichains possesses a chain that meets every antichain in some partition of the poset into antichains.

    (∀ i, IsAntichain (· < ·) (f i)) ∧ (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (f i) (f j)) ∧

directions.title: The Aharoni-Korman Conjecture for Well-Founded FAC Posets

directions.description: Every well-founded partially ordered set satisfying the finite antichain condition (FAC) has the Aharoni-Korman property: there exists a chain C and a partition of the poset into antichains such that C intersects every antichain in the partition. The paper proves the Aharoni-Korman conjecture for countable FAC posets avoiding a specific chain obstruction (saturated chains of the form ⊕_{x∈ω} D_x with each D_x infinite and co-wellfounded). This conjecture extends the result to all well-founded FAC posets, regardless of cardinality, since well-foundedness eliminates infinite descending obstructing chains and structurally constrains ascending ones.

directions.proof_strategy: Stratify the well-founded poset by rank into well-ordered levels. Apply the paper's countable decomposition and scattered poset analysis within each stratum. Use transfinite induction on the rank function to construct the witnessing chain and antichain partition globally, ensuring the chain meets every antichain in the partition at each inductive stage. The key insight is that well-foundedness provides a rank function that naturally organizes the construction and prevents the specific chain obstruction identified in the paper.
directions.title: Aharoni-Korman Property for Well-Founded FAC Posets

directions.description: For any rational polytopal measure P in R^d, the cap-volume function mapping an oriented hyperplane parameterized by (a,b) in R^(d+1) to the volume of P intersected with the halfspace {x | <a, x> <= b} is piecewise rational. Specifically, there exists a finite semialgebraic partition of the parameter space such that on each cell, the cap-volume is given by a rational function of the parameters.

import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
-- Hypothetical imports for semialgebraic geometry and polytopal measures
-- import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Semialgebraic
-- import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Polytope.Rational

variable {d : ℕ} (P : RationalPolytopalMeasure (Fin d → ℝ))

/-- Space of oriented hyperplanes parameterized by normal vector and offset -/
def OrientedHyperplaneSpace := (Fin d → ℝ) × ℝ

/-- Cap volume function: volume of P intersected with the halfspace ⟪a, x⟫ ≤ b -/
noncomputable def capVolume (ab : OrientedHyperplaneSpace) : ℝ :=
  measureReal (P.carrier ∩ {x | ⟪ab.1, x⟫ ≤ ab.2})

/-- The cap-volume function of a rational polytopal measure is piecewise rational. -/
theorem cap_volume_piecewise_rational :
    ∃ (S : Finset (SemialgebraicSet OrientedHyperplaneSpace)) (f : S → RatFunc ℝ),
      (∀ s, ∀ ab ∈ s.1.carrier, capVolume P ab = evalRatFunc (f s) ab) ∧
      (∀ ab : OrientedHyperplaneSpace, ∃ s ∈ S, ab ∈ s.1.carrier) :=
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Define the natural decomposition of the space of oriented hyperplanes based on the combinatorial structure of the intersection P ∩ H_(a,b)^+. Specifically, partition the parameter space into cells where the set of vertices of P lying strictly inside, strictly outside, and on the boundary of the halfspace remains constant. On each such cell, the vertices of the intersection polytope are rational functions of (a,b). Since the volume of a polytope is a sum of determinants of its vertices, the volume function is a rational function of (a,b) on each cell, proving piecewise rationality.
directions.title: Piecewise Rationality of the Polytopal Cap-Volume Function

directions.description: If the Atkin-Lehner quotient of a Shimura curve of level N has genus zero, then the norm of certain algebraic numbers (defined via p-adic cross-ratios of CM points) equals the product conjectured by Giampietro and Darmon.

directions.description: For any integer n >= 11, let a_1 = floor(log_2 n) and t be the number of ones in the binary expansion of n. A non-hook partition of n with at most k parts is an irreducible constituent of the 2-Sylow permutation character of S_n if and only if k <= a_1 + t - 1.

directions.description: For a Δ-matroid on a finite ground set E with feasible set family F, the following are equivalent: (1) the Δ-matroid is strong, i.e., satisfies Wenzel's symmetric exchange property (for all B₁, B₂ ∈ F, if e ∈ B₁ \ B₂ and f ∈ B₂ \ B₁, then there exists g ∈ (B₁ Δ B₂) \ {e,f} such that exactly one of B₁ Δ {e,g} or B₂ Δ {f,g} is in F, or B₁ Δ {e,f} ∈ F and B₂ Δ {e,f} ∈ F); and (2) the Δ-matroid has no peerless antipode (no feasible set B has an antipode A—maximizing |B Δ A|—that is peerless, meaning it is the unique antipode of B satisfying a certain local maximality condition within the antipode system). This equivalence bridges the classical exchange-axiom framework with the novel antipode-combinatorial characterization introduced in the paper.

    {E : Type*} [Fintype E] [DecidableEq E]
    {F : Finset (Finset E)}
    (hF : IsDeltaMatroid F) :
    IsStrongDeltaMatroid F ↔ ¬HasPeerlessAntipode F :=
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Define Δ-matroids, feasible sets, symmetric difference distance, antipodes (feasible sets at maximal symmetric difference from a given feasible set), and peerless antipodes (antipodes that are unique with respect to a local exclusion condition). For the forward direction, show that Wenzel's symmetric exchange prevents the existence of a peerless antipode by demonstrating that any candidate peerless antipode can be exchanged to produce a second distinct antipode violating peerlessness. For the reverse direction, show that a violation of Wenzel's exchange yields a feasible set pair whose antipode structure forces a peerless antipode, by constructing a minimal counterexample and analyzing the antipode configuration around it.
directions.title: Equivalence of Wenzel symmetric exchange and no peerless antipodes for Δ-matroids

directions.description: For the family of series-parallel graphs G(a) obtained by joining two distinguished vertices s and t with m disjoint paths of lengths a_1, ..., a_m, the paper shows that gamma-positivity of the h*-polynomial of Q_G fails for m >= 5. The conjecture is that for m <= 4, gamma-positivity always holds: for every vector a in Z_{>=1}^4, the h*-polynomial of Q_{G(a)} is gamma-positive. This would yield a complete classification of gamma-positivity for this family.

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: For m <= 3, leverage known results: graphs with a vertex connected to all others (cones) are gamma-positive by Ohsugi-Tsuchiya, and complete bipartite graphs by Higashitani-Jochemko-Michalek. For m = 4, compute the gamma-polynomial coefficients using the regular unimodular triangulation structure of symmetric edge polytopes and show all coefficients are non-negative. The linear and quadratic gamma-coefficients are already known positive; the key is controlling the cubic and higher terms via the combinatorics of the series-parallel structure.
directions.title: Gamma-positivity of symmetric edge polytopes for series-parallel graphs with at most four paths

directions.description: For even n ≥ 12, the unique extremal graph with T(n) edges and an edge of non-positive curvature has exactly two vertices of degree n-2 (forming the non-positive curvature edge) and all other vertices have degree n-1. This graph is obtained by removing n/2-2 disjoint edges from K_n such that no two removed edges share a vertex, and the two vertices of degree n-2 are adjacent.

Show that any graph with T(n) edges achieving the threshold must have exactly the specified degree distribution. Prove uniqueness by demonstrating that any two such extremal graphs are isomorphic via vertex relabeling. Use the relationship between graph curvature and Laplacian eigenvalues to constrain the possible structures.
directions.title: Structure of extremal graphs for positive curvature threshold

directions.description: For any natural numbers n, g with n > 2g, the graph whose vertices are chord diagrams (perfect matchings) of genus g on 2n vertices, and whose edges connect diagrams differing by a genus-preserving chord swap, is connected and has diameter at most 100(n + g^2).

Construct explicit sequences of genus-preserving swaps to reduce any diagram to a canonical form, bounding the number of swaps by 100(n + g^2) to establish both connectivity and the explicit diameter bound.

directions.description: The trianguline variety X^{tri}_G associated to a split connected reductive group G over a p-adic field K is Cohen-Macaulay. Specifically, for every point x in X^{tri}_G with local ring O_{X^{tri}_G,x}, the depth equals the Krull dimension: depth(O_{X^{tri}_G,x}) = dim(O_{X^{tri}_G,x}). This extends the paper's results establishing smoothness on the very regular locus and normality at certain points outside this locus, predicting that all singularities are as mild as possible. Cohen-Macaulayness would imply full normality of X^{tri}_G (since CM implies Serre's condition S2, and the smooth locus has complement of codimension ≥ 2 by the regularity conditions on the triangulation parameter), strengthening the paper's partial normality result. It would also have significant consequences for the deformation theory of p-adic Galois representations with G-structure and for understanding the local Langlands correspondence via the geometry of the trianguline variety.

    (X : TriangulineVariety G K) :
    CohenMacaulay X := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: The proof would proceed by analyzing the local structure of the trianguline variety at each point. Key steps: (1) On the very regular locus, the variety is smooth (proven in the paper), hence Cohen-Macaulay. (2) At singular points, use the Tannakian formalism developed in the paper to reduce to understanding the tangent cone in terms of root data. (3) The tangent cone at a singular point with parameter δ should be controlled by the roots α for which δ∘α∨ fails to be regular—these correspond to the walls of the Weyl chambers where smoothness breaks down. (4) Show that the defining ideal at each point is generated by a regular sequence of length equal to the codimension, leveraging the crystallinity criterion from the paper to explicitly describe the deformation ring. (5) The root system combinatorics (specifically, the Chevalley commutation relations and the structure of the unipotent radical) should ensure the regular sequence property holds via an inductive argument on the height of r
directions.title: Cohen-Macaulayness of the Trianguline Variety for Reductive Groups

directions.description: For every simple graph G with maximum degree Δ(G) > |V(G)|/3, the chromatic index χ'(G) equals Δ(G) if and only if G contains no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph (a subgraph H with |E(H)| > Δ(G)·⌊|V(H)|/2⌋). This would yield a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of dense graphs and implies several longstanding conjectures including the 1-Factorization Conjecture for regular graphs.

Prove key lemmas: (1) any Δ-overfull subgraph forces class 2, (2) the Petersen-minus-vertex P* is class 2 with no 3-overfull subgraph (showing Δ > |V|/3 is tight), (3) reduction to Δ-critical graphs. Then apply structural decomposition of critical graphs with Δ > |V|/3 to show they must contain overfull subgraphs, extending known results from Δ ≥ |V|−2 inward.
directions.title: The Overfull Conjecture

directions.description: For a prime p ≠ 2, a finite extension K of Q_p, and a set T = {a₀, b₀, ..., aᵍ, bᵍ} ⊂ P¹(K) of size 2g+2 with g ≥ 1, the set T is in good position (meaning Γ(T) = ⟨s₀,...,sᵍ⟩ is discontinuous and equals the free product ⟨s₀⟩*...*⟨sᵍ⟩, where each sᵢ has order 2 with fixed points {aᵢ,bᵢ}) if and only if: (1) the tree T(T) constructed from the reduction data is a path graph of length 2g+1, and (2) the p-adic valuations of the off-diagonal entries of normalized representatives of the sᵢ satisfy explicit contraction bounds ensuring the generators act as sufficiently contracting maps on the respective complementary residue disks in the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL₂(K).

The backward direction (sufficiency) requires showing that when T(T) is a path of length 2g+1 and the contraction bounds hold, the group Γ(T) is free on the generators sᵢ: one analyzes the action on the Bruhat-Tits tree of PGL₂(K), showing that the contraction conditions force each reduced word in the sᵢ to act without fixed points in Ω_Γ, precluding any relations beyond sᵢ² = 1. The p-adic analytic estimates on matrix entries control how far the generators move points in the Bruhat-Tits tree, ensuring that compositions cannot create accidental fixed points.

directions.description: For a prime power q and positive integer n, the maximum possible codimension h_q(n) of a cyclically covering subspace in F_q^n is zero if and only if every nonzero cyclic code in F_q^n contains a full-weight codeword.

directions.description: For all t ≥ 2 and r ≥ 2, the maximum dimension n for which there exists a line-free r-coloring of the Hales–Jewett cube [t]^n equals the maximum dimension n for which there exists a one-weight (equivalently, symmetric) line-free r-coloring of [t]^n. That is, one-weight colorings are extremal for the lower-bound problem: no arbitrary coloring avoids combinatorial lines in a dimension that no symmetric coloring can.

higher-dimensional combinatorial geometry ↔ integer-weighted counting (via radix weight representation)

Then show that for any line-free r-coloring c of [t]^n, the symmetrization c_sym(x) = c(σ·x) averaged over all coordinate permutations σ ∈ S_n either inherits line-freeness or can be deformed into a one-weight line-free coloring of the same dimension. The key obstacle is that symmetrization may introduce monochromatic lines; resolving this likely requires constructing an explicit radix weight from the orbit structure of c and showing the induced one-weight coloring avoids lines whenever c does. Falsification reduces to a finite computation: find t, r, n and a line-free r-coloring of [t]^n such that no one-weight r-coloring of [t]^n is line-free.

directions.description: The maximum fluctuation of log-microstate counts log Ω_N(E) over energy intervals of width O(√E) in large-N AdS/CFT belongs to the Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating universality class of Gaussian log-correlated fields. Specifically, defining M_N = max_{E ∈ [E₀, E₀ + δ]} log Ω_N(E) with δ ∝ √E₀ and E₀ ∝ N² (the black hole mass scale), the rescaled maximum (M_N - μ_N)/σ_N converges in distribution to a random variable with the modified Gumbel cumulative distribution function exp(-K·exp(-s)), where μ_N = (1/2)·S_N·log(S_N), σ_N = log(S_N), S_N ∝ N² is the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, and K > 0 is a universal constant determined by the log-correlated field covariance structure. This modified Gumbel with logarithmic correction factors distinguishes the FHK universality class from the classical Gumbel extreme value distribution and parallels the original FHK conjecture for max_t log|ζ(1/2+it)| on [0,T].

This strengthens the paper's key observation that V is piecewise rational to the sharper claim that it is piecewise polynomial, with the degree bound d arising from the fact that cap vertices on the hyperplane vary linearly in the hyperplane parameters while simplex volumes are degree-d polynomials in vertex coordinates.

For polytopes, piecewise-rationality of the cap-volume function gives semialgebraicity directly, but for general convex semialgebraic bodies the cap-volume function may not be piecewise rational, so new arguments (e.g., via o-minimal geometry or quantifier elimination over real closed fields with volume integrals) are needed.

This equivalence, proved in the paper for convex polytopes, reveals a fundamental structural identity between a combinatorial-geometric object (centerpoints) and a convex-geometric object (floating bodies). Formalizing even the 2-dimensional case for triangles would require developing substantial infrastructure in convex geometry, measure theory on polytopes, and the centerpoint theorem.

An antipode of a feasible set X ∈ F is a feasible set Y ∈ F such that X and Y are at maximum Hamming distance among all pairs of feasible sets. A peerless antipode is an antipode that is the unique antipode of its partner feasible set. The peerless antipode property bans the existence of any peerless antipode in the system of feasible sets.

Define the symmetric exchange property (strong), the antipode relation via Hamming distance on symmetric difference, and the peerless antipode predicate. The forward direction proceeds by contradiction: assuming a peerless antipode exists, derive a violation of symmetric exchange. The reverse direction uses the peerless antipode property to construct the required exchange elements by showing that any failure of symmetric exchange would produce a peerless antipode configuration. The tropical algebraic motivation via orthogonal Grassmannian tropicalization may provide alternative algebraic proof strategies.

This would sharpen the paper's existence result by establishing the exact threshold, confirming that no smaller counterexamples to the Ohsugi–Tsuchiya conjecture exist.

directions.title: Dimension Threshold for Gamma-Positivity of Symmetric Edge Polytopes

directions.description: For any graph of order n ≥ 8, if it contains strictly more than T(n) = (n^2 - 3n)/2 - ⌈n/2⌉ + 2 edges, then every edge in the graph has strictly positive Ollivier/Lin-Lu-Yau curvature.

    (h_edges : G.edgeFinset.card > T n) :
    ∀ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, linLuYauCurvature G e > 0 := by sorry

Establish structural properties of graphs with non-positive curvature edges, and demonstrate that exceeding the edge threshold T(n) precludes the existence of such subgraphs, thereby forcing all edge curvatures to be strictly positive.
directions.title: Positive Curvature Threshold for Lin-Lu-Yau Curvature

directions.description: For the fixed genus chord swap Markov chain on chord diagrams with n chords and genus g, the spectral gap γ_{n,g} satisfies γ_{n,g} = Θ(n^{-3}) when g is fixed and n → ∞. This sharpens the paper's polynomial lower bound to a precise exponent and matches the n^{-3} scaling observed in related swap chains on perfect matchings.

Then establish the O(n^{-3}) upper bound on the spectral gap via comparison with the random transposition walk on matchings, and prove the Ω(n^{-3}) lower bound by constructing a canonical path argument with congestion bounded by O(n^3), extending the paper's coupling/canonical-path techniques.
directions.title: Tight spectral gap exponent for the fixed-genus chord swap chain

directions.description: Let C be a rigid tensor category and D be a tensor category. Any monoidal natural transformation α : F ⟶ G between two tensor functors F, G : C ⥤ D is an isomorphism. This formalizes Proposition 1.13 of Deligne-Milne, which the paper explicitly invokes to equate the tensor automorphism functor with the tensor homomorphism functor (uAut^⊗ = uHom^⊗) for rigid categories.

theorem isIso_of_monoidal_nat_trans_rigid {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D]
  [MonoidalCategory C] [MonoidalCategory D] [Rigid C] {F G : C ⥤ D}
  [F.Monoidal] [G.Monoidal] (α : F ⟶ G) [α.Monoidal] : IsIso α := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Construct the inverse natural transformation β : G ⟶ F using the duality data of the rigid category C. For an object X in C, define β_X as the composite G(X) ≅ G(X) ⊗ I ⟶ G(X) ⊗ F(Xᵛ ⊗ X) ≅ G(X) ⊗ (F(Xᵛ) ⊗ F(X)) ≅ (G(X) ⊗ F(Xᵛ)) ⊗ F(X) ⟶ (F(Xᵛ) ⊗ G(X)) ⊗ F(X) ⟶ (F(Xᵛ) ⊗ F(X)) ⊗ G(X) ⟶ ... utilizing the evaluation and coevaluation maps of the dual Xᵛ, along with the monoidal structure of F, G, and α. Prove that β is a monoidal natural transformation and the two-sided inverse of α.
directions.title: Rigidity Implies Monoidal Natural Transformations Are Isomorphisms

directions.description: For any odd prime q ≥ 3 and integer m ≥ 4, the maximum codimension of a cyclically covering subspace of 𝔽_q^n, denoted h_q(n), is strictly positive when n = (q^m+1)/2. This is equivalent to the existence of a proper subspace of 𝔽_q^n whose union of cyclic shifts covers the entire vector space.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Card
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Subspace

variable (q m : ℕ)

-- A subspace U of F_q^n is cyclically covering if the union of its cyclic shifts covers F_q^n
def IsCyclicallyCovering {n : ℕ} (U : Submodule (ZMod q) (Fin n → ZMod q)) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : Fin n → ZMod q, ∃ k : Fin n, ∃ u ∈ U, ∀ i : Fin n, v i = u (i + k)

-- h_q(n) > 0 is equivalent to the existence of a proper cyclically covering subspace
theorem h_q_pos_for_qm_plus_1_over_2 (hq : q ≥ 3) (hm : m ≥ 4) (h_prime : Nat.Prime q) :
    ∃ (U : Submodule (ZMod q) (Fin ((q^m + 1) / 2) → ZMod q)), 
      U ≠ ⊤ ∧ IsCyclicallyCovering U := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Translate the condition h_q(n) > 0 into the existence of a non-zero cyclic code without a full-weight codeword. Explicitly construct such a cyclic code in 𝔽_q^n for n = (q^m+1)/2 by defining its generator polynomial using the properties of the multiplicative group of 𝔽_{q^m}, and prove that no codeword in this code has full weight.
directions.title: Positivity of Cyclically Covering Subspace Codimension for (q^m+1)/2

directions.description: Every symmetric r-coloring of the Hales-Jewett cube [t]^n — one invariant under all coordinate permutations of the word — is a one-weight coloring: there exist integer weights w_1, ..., w_t such that the color of a word x ∈ [t]^n depends only on the weighted sum ∑_i w_{x_i}. Conversely, every one-weight coloring is symmetric. This equivalence reduces the symmetric lower-bound problem for Hales-Jewett numbers to the d=1 case of Gallai's theorem on homothetic copies of a t-point set in Z.
domain_bridges: Integer-weighted letter sums as complete invariants
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem symmetric_iff_oneweight {t n r : ℕ} (ht : 1 ≤ t) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (c : (Fin n → Fin t) → Fin r) : is_symmetric_coloring c ↔ ∃ (w : Fin t → ℤ) (f : ℤ → Fin r), ∀ x : Fin n → Fin t, c x = f (∑ i : Fin n, w (x i))
directions.proof_strategy: The forward direction (one-weight ⇒ symmetric) is immediate since permuting coordinates preserves the multiset of letters and hence the weighted sum. For the converse, given a symmetric coloring c, construct the radix weight by examining how c distinguishes words that differ only in letter substitution: define w_j - w_1 as the minimal coordinate substitution that changes the color class when swapping a letter 1 for letter j in a fixed position. Show that the orbit of any word under coordinate permutations is determined by its letter-count vector, and that c factors through the weighted sum because symmetry forces c to depend only on the letter-count, which the radix weight encodes injectively modulo the kernel of c. The key combinatorial lemma is that the color partition of Z induced by the weighted sum is well-defined and independent of the choice of representative word.
directions.title: Symmetric Colorings of Hales-Jewett Cubes Coincide with One-Weight Colorings

directions.description: A class of finite graphs is homomorphism distinguishing closed if and only if it is closed under homomorphic equivalence, disjoint unions, and taking split-off minors. This conjecture proposes a corrected version of the Strong Roberson Conjecture by substituting the minor relation with the newly introduced split-off minor relation.
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem hom_distinguishing_closed_iff_split_off_minor_closed (C : GraphClass) : IsHomDistinguishingClosed C ↔ IsClosedUnderHomEquiv C ∧ IsClosedUnderDisjointUnions C ∧ IsClosedUnderSplitOffMinors C := by sorry
directions.proof_strategy: For the backward direction, generalize the existing proof that closure under split-off minors and disjoint unions implies homomorphism distinguishing closed. For the forward direction, assume a class is homomorphism distinguishing closed and demonstrate it must be closed under split-off minors by showing that if G is a split-off minor of F in the class, excluding G would alter the homomorphism indistinguishability relation, leveraging the connection between oddomorphisms and split-off minors.
directions.title: Split-Off Minor Characterization of Homomorphism Distinguishing Closed Classes

directions.description: An irreducible polynomial F in K[x_1,...,x_d] over an algebraically closed field K of characteristic zero is algebraically degenerate (i.e., F divides a sum of non-constant univariate polynomials f_1(x_1)+...+f_d(x_d)) if and only if there exist non-zero polynomials G and univariate alpha_{1,j}, alpha_{2,i} such that for each i, the partial derivative F_{x_i} is congruent to G * alpha_{2,i}(x_i) * prod_{j!=i} alpha_{1,j}(x_j) modulo F. This translates the local analytic characterization of Theorem 2.3 into a global algebraic setting.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
theorem global_algebraic_degeneracy_criterion
    {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsAlgClosed K]
    {d : ℕ} {F : MvPolynomial (Fin d) K} (hF : Irreducible F) :
    (∃ f : Fin d → Polynomial K, ∀ i, (f i).degree > 0 ∧ 
      F ∣ ∑ i : Fin d, univariate_comp i (f i)) ↔
    (∃ (G : MvPolynomial (Fin d) K) (α1 α2 : Fin d → Polynomial K),
       ∀ i : Fin d, 
         F ∣ (MvPolynomial.pderiv i F - 
           G * univariate_comp i (α2 i) * 
           ∏ j : Fin d, if j = i then 1 else univariate_comp j (α1 j)))
directions.proof_strategy: Adapt the local analytic proof from the paper to the global algebraic setting using properties of algebraic curves and irreducibility, leveraging the fact that for polynomials over algebraically closed fields, local divisibility implies global divisibility, and applying Hilbert's Nullstellensatz to bridge the local zero sets to the global ideal structure.
directions.title: Global Algebraic Degeneracy Criterion for Multivariate Polynomials

directions.description: Theorem 2.3 of the referenced paper establishes that an irreducible polynomial $F \in \mathbb{R}[x_1, \ldots, x_d]$ is degenerate if and only if, near each coordinate regular point $p \in Z(F)$, the partial derivatives admit a separated analytic factorization $F_{x_i} = G \cdot \alpha_{2,i}(x_i) \prod_{j \neq i} \alpha_{1,j}(x_j)$ on $Z(F)$, where $G$ and $\alpha_{k,j}$ are real analytic. This conjecture asserts that when $F$ is degenerate, the analytic factorization can be promoted to a global polynomial congruence: there exist polynomials $\tilde{G} \in \mathbb{R}[x_1, \ldots, x_d]$ and $\tilde{\alpha}_{k,j} \in \mathbb{R}[t]$ such that $F_{x_k} \equiv \tilde{G} \cdot \tilde{\alpha}_{2,k}(x_k) \cdot \prod_{j \neq k} \tilde{\alpha}_{1,j}(x_j) \pmod{\langle F \rangle}$ for each $k = 1, \ldots, d$. This would yield a purely algebraic (and effectively computable) criterion for degeneracy, replacing the local analytic characterization with a global polynomial one.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
theorem polynomial_separated_factorization_of_degenerate
    {d : ℕ} (hd : d ≥ 3)
    (F : MvPolynomial (Fin d) ℝ) (hF_irred : Irreducible F)
    (hF_degen : IsDegenerate F)
    : ∃ (G : MvPolynomial (Fin d) ℝ)
        (α₁ α₂ : Fin d → Polynomial ℝ),
      ∀ k : Fin d,
        ∃ H : MvPolynomial (Fin d) ℝ,
        (MvPolynomial.pderiv k F)
        = G * (α₂ k).toMvPolynomial k
          * ∏ j : {j : Fin d // j ≠ k}, (α₁ j).toMvPolynomial j
        + F * H
-- where IsDegenerate encodes the analytic definition from the paper
-- and (α₂ k).toMvPolynomial k embeds the univariate polynomial
-- as a multivariate polynomial depending only on variable k
directions.proof_strategy: Since $F$ is irreducible, $\langle F \rangle$ is prime and the quotient $R = \mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/\langle F \rangle$ is an integral domain whose fraction field $K$ embeds into the field of meromorphic functions on any Zariski-open subset of the smooth locus of $Z(F)$. The analytic factorization from Theorem 2.3 forces each $\alpha_{i,j}$, viewed as a function on $Z(F)$, to satisfy algebraic relations over $K$. Since $F_{x_i} \in R$ and the factorization holds identically on an open dense subset, the $\alpha_{i,j}$ must be rational functions on $Z(F)$, hence elements of $K$. Clearing denominators yields the polynomial congruence modulo $F$. The key subtlety is ensuring the single-variable structure is preserved when lifting from analytic to algebraic, which requires showing that if a rational function on $Z(F)$ restricts to a function of $x_j$ alone on a Zariski-dense set, then it equals a rational function of $x_j$ in $K$.
directions.title: Polynomial Lifting of the Separated Factorization for Degenerate Polynomials

directions.description: For all finite graphs F and G, there exists an oddomorphism from F to G if and only if G is a split-off minor of F. The forward direction is established in the paper; the converse remains open.
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem oddomorphism_iff_split_off_minor (F G : SimpleGraph) [Fintype V_F] [Fintype V_G] [DecidableRel (Adj F)] [DecidableRel (Adj G)] : Oddomorphism F G ↔ IsSplitOffMinor G F := by sorry
directions.proof_strategy: The forward direction is given by the paper's Theorem that oddomorphism from F to G implies G is a split-off minor of F. For the converse, attempt to construct an oddomorphism from F to G given that G is a split-off minor of F, by reversing each split-off minor operation step and verifying parity conditions on homomorphism counts are preserved. A counterexample search via CFI-type constructions could also be pursued.
directions.title: Equivalence of Oddomorphism and Split-Off Minor

directions.description: For any field K with char(K) ≠ 2 and quadratic polynomials v, w ∈ K[x], the classical Wronskian v'w - vw' is exactly equal to the derivative-free Remainder-Polynomial Route (RPR) formulation. Specifically, v'w - vw' = 2x · Sres₁(v, w) + (v₁w - w₁v), where Sres₁(v,w) = v₂w - w₂v is the first subresultant of v and w, and vᵢ, wᵢ are the coefficients of xⁱ in v, w respectively. This identity generalizes symmetrically to the full Richelot triple (U, V, W), proving that RPR yields identical codomain polynomials not merely up to scalar units, but as an exact polynomial equality.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.Derivative

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] (v w : K[X])

theorem rpr_exact_identity (hchar : (2 : K) ≠ 0) (hv : v.natDegree ≤ 2) (hw : w.natDegree ≤ 2) :
    Polynomial.deriv v * w - v * Polynomial.deriv w =
    2 * (Polynomial.X : K[X]) * (v.coeff 2 • w - w.coeff 2 • v) +
    (v.coeff 1 • w - w.coeff 1 • v) := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Expand both sides of the identity v'w - vw' = 2x(v₂w - w₂v) + (v₁w - w₁v) using the standard definition of the formal derivative v' = 2v₂x + v₁. Distributing the terms on the right-hand side and collecting coefficients of x², x, and 1 directly yields the expanded left-hand side, (v₂w₁ - v₁w₂)x² + 2(v₂w₀ - v₀w₂)x + (v₁w₀ - v₀w₁), proving the exact polynomial equality purely through algebraic manipulation without relying on scalar units or characteristic restrictions beyond char(K) ≠ 2.
directions.title: Exact Identity of Wronskian and Subresultant Richelot Formulations

directions.description: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let F ∈ k[x₁,…,x_d] be irreducible. Then F = H(f₁(x₁)+⋯+f_d(x_d)) for some H ∈ k[t] with deg(H) ≥ 2 and fᵢ ∈ k[t] if and only if there exist rational functions α₁,ⱼ ∈ k(xⱼ), α₂,ᵢ ∈ k(xᵢ), and G ∈ k(x₁,…,x_d) such that for every i ∈ {1,…,d}: ∂F/∂xᵢ ≡ G · α₂,ᵢ(xᵢ) · ∏_{j≠i} α₁,ⱼ(xⱼ) (mod ⟨F⟩), where crucially the α₁,ⱼ factors are independent of i. This is the algebraic analogue of Theorem 2.3, replacing analytic isomorphisms with rational function substitutions and local neighborhoods with Zariski-open conditions.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
theorem algebraic_degeneracy_criterion {d : ℕ} {k : Type*} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
    (F : MVPolynomial (Fin d) k) (hF : Irreducible F) :
    (∃ (H : Polynomial k) (f : Fin d → Polynomial k),
      H.natDegree ≥ 2 ∧
      F = (MVPolynomial.map (Polynomial.sum fun i => (f i).comp' (MVPolynomial.X i))) H) ↔
    (∃ (G : MVPolynomial (Fin d) k) (α₁ α₂ : Fin d → MVPolynomial (Fin d) k),
      (∀ j, (α₁ j).vars ⊆ {j}) ∧
      (∀ i, (α₂ i).vars ⊆ {i}) ∧
      ∀ i, F.partialDeriv i - G * α₂ i * (∏ j in Finset.univ.erase i, α₁ j)
        ∈ Ideal.span {F}) := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Forward direction: If F = H(f₁+⋯+f_d), then ∂F/∂xᵢ = H'(f₁+⋯+f_d)·f'ᵢ(xᵢ). On Z(F) where H(f₁+⋯+f_d)=0, set G = H'(f₁+⋯+f_d), α₂,ᵢ = f'ᵢ, α₁,ⱼ = 1. Reverse direction: The separated factorization implies F_{x_i}/F_{x_j} = (α₂,ᵢ(xᵢ)·α₁,ⱼ(xⱼ))/(α₂,ⱼ(xⱼ)·α₁,ᵢ(xᵢ)), forcing the logarithmic derivatives ∂(log F_{x_i})/∂x_j to vanish modulo F for i≠j. Use irreducibility and Zariski density to show the implicit function on Z(F) has additive separable structure, then integrate via differential algebra (Risch-like arguments) to obtain the polynomial form H(f₁+⋯+f_d).
directions.title: Algebraic Degeneracy Factorization Criterion

directions.description: For any generalized star configuration ideal I of height h defined by n ≥ h+1 forms f₁,…,fₙ in a polynomial ring over a field, where any h of the forms constitute a regular sequence, the standard Veronese degree svd(I) equals lcm(1, 2, …, h). This extends the paper's main theorem for monomial star configurations to the generalized setting, predicting that the Veronese degree depends only on h, not on the specific choice of forms or the ambient polynomial ring.

    (hreg : ∀ s : Finset (Fin n), s.card = h → IsRegularSeq (s.map forms))
    (I : Ideal (Polynomial k))
    (hI : I = ⨅ s : Finset (Fin n), (_ : s.card = h) → Ideal.span (s.map forms)) :
    svd I = Finset.lcm (Finset.Icc 1 h) id :=

Then extend to generalized star configurations by showing the Diophantine structure governing symbolic powers is invariant under regular sequences of forms—potentially via initial ideal arguments preserving svd, or by establishing that the symbolic Rees algebra of a generalized star configuration has the same Veronese structure as its monomial specialization.
directions.title: Standard Veronese Degree of Generalized Star Configurations Equals lcm(1,…,h)

directions.description: For any prime power q and integers 2 ≤ m ≤ n, the multilinear forms Cayley graph Γ(F_q^{2×m×n}) generated by rank-one tensors has exactly m+1 distinct eigenvalues, in one-to-one correspondence with the possible ranks r ∈ {0, 1, ..., m} of m×n matrices over F_q. This generalizes the complete spectrum computation for 2×3×3 tensors established in the paper, where m=3 yields 4 distinct eigenvalues determined by the rank distribution of 3×3 matrices. Despite the graph failing to be distance-regular for order-3 tensors, the spectral structure for the 2×m×n format remains governed entirely by the rank-metric code distribution.
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem multilinear_cayley_distinct_eigenvalue_count {q m n : ℕ} (hq : IsPrimePower q) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ n) : Finset.card (Set.finsetOfDistinctEigenvalues (multilinearFormsCayleyGraph q (2, m, n))) = m + 1 := by sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Extend the recursive spectral analysis from the 2×3×3 case to general 2×m×n format by decomposing the character sum over rank-one tensors according to the rank profile of the corresponding m×n matrix slice, leveraging the established connection between tensor subspace intersections with the Segre variety and the rank distribution of the associated rank-metric codes. The key step is showing that characters indexed by tensors whose m×n slices have equal rank produce identical eigenvalues, yielding exactly m+1 distinct spectral values.
directions.title: Distinct Eigenvalue Count for 2×m×n Multilinear Forms Cayley Graphs

directions.description: For any non-degenerate homogeneous quadratic form Q in 3 variables over ℤ whose zero set in ℙ²(ℚ) is nonempty, the dynamical system on [0,1] constructed by applying Romik's stereographic projection method to the Berggren tree of Q is ergodic and conservative with respect to its absolutely continuous invariant measure obtained via Keane's adaptation.

  sorry

Show T_Q admits a Markov partition with the Gibbs-Markov property. Compute the invariant density using Keane's method (tracking how the quadratic form coefficients transform under the Berggren matrices). Apply the Hopf argument adapted to infinite measure spaces to establish ergodicity, and verify conservativity via the ratio ergodic theorem by checking integrability of the density against the return time function.
directions.title: Ergodicity of Dynamical Systems Induced from Berggren Trees

directions.description: For natural numbers y > 2 and m > 1, the sequence defined by the initial value x_0 = 2^(1 + floor(ceil(log2 y) / m)) and the integer Newton-Raphson iteration x_{i+1} = x_i + floor((y - x_i^m) / (m * x_i^(m-1))) converges to the floor of y^(1/m). Specifically, there exists a natural number k such that for all j >= k, x_j = floor(y^(1/m)).

  ∃ k, ∀ j ≥ k, int_nr_seq y m j hy hm = ⌊(y : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m : ℝ))⌋ := by sorry

Then, prove by induction that the sequence monotonically decreases and remains greater than or equal to floor(y^(1/m)) until it reaches a fixed point. Finally, show that the only fixed point of the iteration in this range is floor(y^(1/m)).
directions.title: Convergence and Correctness of Integer Newton-Raphson for Integer Roots

directions.description: For any simple graph G with n vertices and m edges, and for any 1 ≤ k ≤ n-1, the sum of the k largest Laplacian eigenvalues s_k(G) equals m + binom(k+1, 2) if and only if G is a threshold graph with clique number k+1.

    (n m k : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (h_m : G.edgeCount = m) (h_k : 0 < k ∧ k < n) :
    sum_k_largest_laplacian_eigenvalues G k = m + (k + 1) * k / 2 ↔
    IsThresholdGraph G ∧ CliqueNumber G = k + 1 := by sorry

Show that equality in Brouwer's bound implies equality in Grone-Merris-Bai, forcing the degree sequence to match the Laplacian eigenvalue sequence. Use the characterization of threshold graphs via their degree sequences and the specific sum m + binom(k+1, 2) to conclude that G must be a threshold graph with clique number k+1.
directions.title: Full Brouwer's Laplacian Conjecture Equality Characterization

directions.description: For every positive integer n and positive reals α, β with αβ = π², the alternating Hurwitz zeta function ζ_E(s, x) = Σ_{k=0}^∞ (-1)^k / (k + x)^s satisfies a Ramanujan-type identity generalizing Ramanujan's classical formula for ζ(2n+1). Specifically, the alternating Hurwitz kernel K_E^{2n+1}(α, x) := ½ζ_E(2n+1, x) + Σ_{m=1}^∞ m^{-2n-1}/(e^{2αm} + 1) obeys: α^{-n}·K_E^{2n+1}(α, x) − (−β)^{-n}·K_E^{2n+1}(β, 1−x) = 2^{2n} Σ_{k=0}^{n+1} (−1)^{k−1} E_{2k}(x) B_{2n−2k+2} / ((2k)!(2n−2k+2)!) · α^{n−k+1} β^k, where E_{2k}(x) are Euler polynomials and B_{2k} are Bernoulli numbers. This replaces the Bernoulli numbers B_{2k} in Ramanujan's original identity with Euler polynomials E_{2k}(x), reflecting the alternating (sign-twisted) structure.

theorem alternating_hurwitz_ramanujan (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≥ 1) (α β x : ℝ) (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 0 < β) (hab : α * β = π^2) (hx : 0 < x) (hx1 : x < 1) :
  let K := λ s a t, (1/2 : ℝ) * alternatingHurwitzZeta s t + ∑' m, (m : ℝ)^(-s) / (Real.exp (2 * a * m) + 1) in
  α^(-n : ℝ) * K (2*n+1) α x - (-β)^(-n : ℝ) * K (2*n+1) β (1 - x)

This rules out A₅, S₅, F₂₀ (Frobenius group of order 20), and all other transitive subgroups of S₅ as geometric monodromy groups for such functions.

This provides an explicit constant in the O(log n) bound established for related families in the paper, extending the probabilistic method of Babai to the directed tournament setting with a constructive resolvability guarantee.

Use the strong regularity properties to bound this probability below 1/n², then take a union bound over all pairs. This conjecture asserts that 'sufficiently large' can be replaced by the explicit threshold n ≥ k. Note that for n ≤ k the whole grid has no k+1 collinear points so f_k(n) = n², and for n = k we get f_k(k) = k² = k·k, making n ≥ k the natural boundary. The conjecture predicts that for all k ≥ 3 and n ≥ k, the trivial upper bound kn is always achievable.

A computer-verified case analysis for small n (up to some explicit bound) combined with the asymptotic argument for larger n could work. The key is determining whether the o(n) deletion/swinging losses can be controlled when n is close to k.

The case m=3 appears in the paper as a key lemma simplifying the Bogart–Longyear formula for L_{3,n}, and the case m=2 is the classical Chu–Vandermonde identity. The general form underpins Gessel's formula for m-row Latin rectangles and its 3D rook polynomial generalization.

directions.description: For every number field K with ring of integers O_K, and every effective divisor D on the open unit disk 𝔻, there exists a holomorphic function f on 𝔻 whose Taylor coefficients all lie in O_K (viewed as a subring of ℂ via a fixed embedding σ : K ↪ ℂ) and whose zero divisor is exactly D. This directly generalizes the paper's Theorem 2.1 (the Gaussian-integer case O_K = ℤ[i]) to arbitrary rings of integers. The paper's proof for ℤ[i] exploits the Euclidean domain structure for an inductive rounding scheme; for general O_K, the full-rank lattice structure O_K ≅ ℤ^n should permit analogous nearest-lattice-point rounding within the jet-correction framework, but the non-uniqueness of rounding in non-Euclidean rings introduces subtleties that require new arguments.

Step 3: Verify that the triangular structure of the coefficient map and the convergence bounds from canonical-product theory carry through unchanged, since the lattice rounding errors are bounded by the covering radius of O_K.

The paper establishes the asymptotic bound m_d ≤ 1/2 + O(1/d), but the exact value m_d = 1/2 remains open.

This extends the paper's main result, which establishes the case ω = 1 via approximate concentration (for ε small enough, the values are forced to equal 1 since μ_k is discrete). The case of general ω does not reduce to ω = 1 by a simple substitution, as f(n)/ω is not completely multiplicative, making this a genuinely stronger statement that implies every color class of a completely multiplicative k-coloring of ℕ contains a Pythagorean triple.

directions.description: For finite simple graphs G and H on disjoint vertex sets, the matching number of their join G∗H satisfies ν(G∗H) = min(ν(G) + |V(H)|, ν(H) + |V(G)|, ⌊(|V(G)| + |V(H)|)/2⌋). This is the foundational combinatorial theorem of the paper, proved via the Tutte-Berge formula, and underpins all subsequent results on squarefree powers of edge ideals of wheel, fan, and friendship graphs.

The key observation is that every vertex of V(H) not in S is adjacent to every vertex of V(G) not in S_G, so odd components of (G∗H) - S arise only from odd components of G - S_G together with the complete bipartite structure of the join. Formalizing it requires developing the theories of generic representations of GL_r over p-adic fields, both integral-representation (Jacquet–Shalika) and Langlands–Shahidi constructions of L- and ε-factors, and the local functional equation for the Jacquet–Shalika exterior square integrals.

directions.description: Let z and X be indeterminates. Define the two polynomials in t: f(t) = z(t+256)^3 - 1728t^2 and g(t) = X(t+64)^2 - 256t, viewed as elements of (Z[z,X])[t]. Define the bridge polynomial Φ(z,X) = 729z²X³ + 3888z²X² + 6912z²X + 4096z² - 1458zX³ + 22356zX² - 27648zX + 729X³. Then the resultant of f and g with respect to t equals 2^36 · Φ(z,X). This identity is the algebraic backbone of the paper, establishing the explicit polynomial relation between the level-one j-invariant parameter z = 1728/j and the Fricke parameter X = 256t/(t+64)², and is verified by a direct resultant computation.

This conjecture posits that the constant 4 in the exponent is an artifact of the Fermat number construction and can be replaced by any arbitrarily small epsilon > 0, yielding a lower bound of x * exp(-ε * (logloglogx / loglogx) * logx). This would substantially bridge the gap to Erdős's grand challenge conjecture that N(x) > c_0 * x for some constant c_0 > 0.

directions.description: The number of length-n quasinecklaces Q_k(n) is exactly k times the number of length-n necklaces N_k(n) for all k ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1.
directions.proof_strategy: Demonstrate that each necklace corresponds to exactly k quasinecklaces via rotational symmetry or quasinecklace construction rules.
directions.title: Proportionality of quasinecklaces to necklaces

directions.description: Every exceptional rational function of degree 5 over F_q, where char(F_q) ∉ {2, 5}, is Möbius-equivalent to exactly one of four families: (1) the monomial X^5 (cyclic monodromy, single branch point), (2) a Rédei function of degree 5 (cyclic monodromy, two branch points), (3) a Dickson polynomial D_5(X, a) for some a ∈ F_q^× (dihedral monodromy with an F_q-rational branch point), or (4) a specific non-polynomial rational function arising from a rational 5-isogeny of an elliptic curve (dihedral monodromy without F_q-rational branch point). The monodromy group structure (cyclic vs. dihedral) and branch point rationality completely determine the function type.

directions.proof_strategy: Formalize the key definitions: exceptional rational functions (permuting P^1(F_{q^m}) for infinitely many m via the Fried–Schur–Saxon criterion), Möbius equivalence, and arithmetic/geometric monodromy groups as permutation groups on 5 elements. Case-split by geometric monodromy group: cyclic case uses classification of transitive cyclic subgroups of S_5 with Riemann–Hurwitz constraining ramification to yield monomials and Rédei functions; dihedral case analyzes inertia subgroups of D_5 within S_5 and branch point rationality to derive Dickson polynomials and the elliptic isogeny family. Key intermediate lemma: for degree 5, the Riemann–Hurwitz formula restricts the possible ramification configurations to finitely many cases for each monodromy type.
directions.title: Classification of Exceptional Rational Functions of Degree 5 over Finite Fields

catalog_references: Exact enumeration of lozenge tilings of a triangular region
directions.description: The paper gives an exact product formula for the number of lozenge tilings T_n of a triangular region T_n involving complex roots of unity: T_n = ∏_{1≤a<b≤3n+2, (a,b)≠(n+1,2n+2)} |1+ζ^a+ζ^b|^{1/3} with ζ = e^{2πi/(3n+3)}. This conjecture states that this complicated product simplifies to a product of binomial coefficients: T_n = ∏_{k=1}^n (3k-1 choose k). This is a precise, falsifiable identity that can be checked for small n and would provide a much simpler closed form.

One could attempt to simplify the product of these eigenvalues using trigonometric identities and known product formulas for binomial coefficients. Alternatively, compute T_n for small n to guess the recurrence, then prove the recurrence holds for the binomial product and matches the determinant formula via creative telescoping or the holonomic systems approach.
directions.title: Simplified binomial product formula for lozenge tilings of the triangular region T_n

directions.description: For every doubly regular tournament T on n vertices (where n ≡ 3 mod 4, n ≥ 3), the metric dimension β(T) ≤ 2⌈log₂ n⌉. This extends the paper's O(log n) bound proven for certain doubly regular team tournaments to the classical and well-studied family of doubly regular tournaments, which are regular tournaments with parameters (n, (n-1)/2, (n-3)/4). The conjecture posits an explicit constant of 2, making it directly falsifiable by computing metric dimensions of small doubly regular tournaments (n = 3, 7, 11, 19, ...) and checking against the bound.

  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Adapt Babai's probabilistic method as used in the paper: for a doubly regular tournament T, randomly sample k = 2⌈log₂ n⌉ vertices as a resolving set candidate. Compute the probability that two distinct vertices u, v receive the same distance vector from the sampled set. Use the strong regularity properties of doubly regular tournaments—specifically that every pair of vertices has exactly (n-3)/4 common out-neighbours—to bound the collision probability per pair by 1/2^k. Apply a union bound over all n(n-1)/2 pairs, choosing k so that the union bound is < 1, yielding a resolving set of size at most 2⌈log₂ n⌉.
directions.title: Logarithmic metric dimension of doubly regular tournaments

directions.description: Let adj be an irreflexive directed adjacency relation on n vertices (encoded as a predicate on Fin n × Fin n, with opposite arcs u→v and v→u both allowed). If the resulting digraph contains no directed triangle (no u→v→w→u), then the total number of arcs is at most ⌊n²/2⌋. This is the key combinatorial ingredient used in the paper to bound the measure of spherical sets avoiding x+y+z=0 via a probabilistic argument over SO(d), and it generalizes Mantel's theorem to directed graphs.

The degree bound follows from the observation that for any arc x→y, the in-neighborhood of x and out-neighborhood of y are disjoint (else a directed triangle exists).

directions.description: The paper proves that for $k \ge 3$ and sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a subset of the $n \times n$ grid with no $k+1$ collinear points is exactly $kn$. This conjecture posits that the condition 'sufficiently large $n$' can be relaxed to $n > k$, meaning $f_k(n) = kn$ holds for all $k \ge 3$ and $n > k$. This would unify the trivial case ($n \le k$, where $f_k(n) = n^2$) and the asymptotic regime.

This strengthens the paper's Theorem 1, which guarantees a positive proportion depending on m, by asserting the proportion does not decay to zero as m → ∞.

directions.description: For all natural numbers m, a, and d, the sum over all m-tuples (i_1, ..., i_m) of non-negative integers summing to d of the product of binomial coefficients ∏_{j=1}^{m} C(a + i_j, a) equals C(ma + d + m - 1, d). This generalizes the identity stated in the paper for m=3 (used to simplify the Bogart-Longyear formula for 3-row Latin rectangles), where the paper claims it is 'easily proved with dots and dividers.' The generalization connects directly to Gessel's framework through multisymmetric function generating series.
